Vehicles Act, 1988, Against The Judgment And Award
Dated 31.10.2019 Passed In Mvc No.854/2016 On The File
Of The Additional Senior Civil Judge And Motor
Accident Claims Tribunal, Ranebennur, Partly
Allowing The Claim Petition For Compensation And
Seeking Enhancement Of Compensation.

This Mfa Coming On For Further Hearing This
Day, The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The claimant in MVC No.854 of 2016 on the file of the learned Additional Senior Civil Judge and AMACT, Ranebennur (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribnunal' for brevity), is impugning the judgment and award dated 31.10.1999, awarding compensation of Rs.6,13,600/- with interest at 7%
per annum from the date of petition till its realisation.
2. Parties are referred to as per their rank and status before the Tribunal.
3. Brief facts of the case are that, the claimant has claimed compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that occurred on 13.11.2015.
It is NC: 2023:KHC-D:7429 contended that on the fateful day, the claimant was riding the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-17/TQ-2037.

In the meantime, the tractor trailer bearing registration No.KA-17/TC- 6603 and 6604 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the motor cycle ridden by the claimant, as a result of which, he sustained grievous injury and was shifted to C.G Hospital,
Davangere.
He has taken treatment as inpatient and thereafter shifted to KIMS Hospital, Manipal.
The claimant underwent surgery and implants were also inserted.
He suffered permanent disability and spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
Therefore, respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the tractor trailer in question are liable to pay compensation.

Accordingly, he prayed for allowing the petition.
4.
Respondent No.1 filed the objections denying the contention taken by the claimant.
It is contended that the claimant himself was negligent in riding the motor cycle.
Therefore, he is not entitled for compensation from respondent No.1.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:7429 Sri.Shivu @ Shivamurthi S/O ... vs Sri.Shekharappa S/O Doddaveerappa on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172825066/
2 5. Respondent No.2 filed the objections taking similar contention and denying the entitlement of compensation to the claimant.

6. On the basis of these pleadings, the Trial Court framed the following issues and additional issue for consideration:
"1. Whether petitioners prove that the accident in question was occurred on 13.11.2015 at about 15.45 hours, near Maganahalli gate on Harapanahalli road, due to the rash and negligent driving of the vehicle TT Unit bearing Reg.No.KA- 17/TC-6603 and 6604 by its driver?
2. Whether the respondent No.1 proves his discharge from the liability for the grounds urged in his written statement?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled to claim compensation as prayed for?

If so,
from whom and at what rate?
4.
What order or award?

Additional issues:
1. Whether the respondent No.2 proves its discharge from the liability for the grounds urged in its written statement?"
NC: 2023:KHC-D:7429 7.
The claimant examined himself as PW1 and examined PWs.2 to 4 and got marked Exs.P1 to 169 in support of his contention.
Respondents have not led any evidence nor got marked any documents.

The Tribunal after taking into consideration all the materials on record, answered issue Nos.1 and 2 in the Affirmative, issue No.3 partly in affirmative and additional issue No.1 in the Negative and awarded compensation of Rs.6,13,600/- with interest at 7% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
8.
Being aggrieved by the same, the claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.
9. Heard Sri Chandrashekar M Hosamani, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri Subhash J Baddi, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Perused the materials on record including the Trial Court records.
10. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that accident is of the year 2015.
The Tribunal has taken the income of the injured at Rs.6,000/- per month.
The income of the injured could have been taken atleast at Rs.8,000/- per NC: 2023:KHC-D:7429 month.
The Tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards loss of amenities and the compensation awarded under other heads are very Sri.

Shivu @ Shivamurthi S/O ... vs Sri.Shekharappa S/O Doddaveerappa on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172825066/
3 meager.
Therefore, the same is to be enhanced.
Accordingly, he prays for allowing the appeal.

11. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 opposing the appeal submitted that, the documents that are placed before the Tribunal were considered in the right perspective and just compensation is already awarded.
There is no scope for enhancement.
He further submits that the Tribunal without any basis has awarded 7% per annum, hence, he prays for reducing the rate of interest to 6% per annum and pass appropriate orders.

12. In view of the rival contentions urged by learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal suffers from infirmity and calls for any interference by this Court?"
NC: 2023:KHC-D:7429

My answer to the above point is in 'partly in affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 13.
The claimant was aged 30 years and he is said to be a businessman.
The accident had occurred on 13.11.2015.
The claimant has not produced any material to prove his income.

Under such circumstances, the guidelines issued for reckoning the compensation before the Lok Adalath could be taken into consideration and the income of the injured can be considered at Rs.8,000/- per month.
As per Ex.P12 - the wound certificate, the claimant has suffered three fractures.
The medical records disclose that he underwent treatment as inpatient for a period of 43 days.
He underwent surgery and implants were also implanted.
PWs.3 and 4 are the doctors who have treated the claimant and deposed before the Court.
Ex . P15
is the disability certificate, according to which, the claimant has suffered partial permanent disablement at 66%.
The Tribunal has assessed the partial disablement at 25%, which is just and reasonable.

Considering the nature of injury, NC:
2023:KHC-D:7429 duration of treatment and the disability suffered by the claimant, he is entitled for future medical expenses.
14.

Therefore, the claimant is entitled to the compensation as under:
Sl. Awarded by this  Particulars No. Court in Rs.

1 Pain and suffering 40,000/-
2 Loss of amenities 30,000/-
3 Loss of income during laid up 24,000/-
 period (8000 x 3)
4

Future loss of income 3,84,000/-
 (8000 x 12 x 25/100 x 16)
5

Medical Expenses 2,72,100/-
6 Conveyance, attendant charges 25,000/-
Sri.Shivu @ Shivamurthi S/O ... vs Sri.Shekharappa S/O Doddaveerappa on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172825066/
4  and other incidental charges 7

Future medical expenses 25,000/-
 TOTAL 8,00,100/-
15.

Hence, the claimant is entitled to the compensation of Rs.8,00,100/- as against Rs.6,13,600/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
The Tribunal has awarded rate of interest at 7% per annum without assigning any reason.
Therefore, the claimant is entitled for interest at 6% per annum for the enhanced amount.

Accordingly, I answer the above point in partly in affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The judgment and award dated 31.10.1999 passed in MVC No.854 of 2016 on the file of learned Additional Senior Civil Judge and AMACT, Ranebennur, is hereby modified.
(iii) The appellant-claimant is entitled for the compensation of Rs.8,01,000/- instead of Rs.6,13,600/- as awarded by the Tribunal.
(iv) The claimant is entitled for interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced compensation from the date of petition till realization.
Other findings of the Tribunal remains intact.
Registry is directed to draw the decree accordingly.
The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal, forthwith.
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7429 Registry to send back the Trial court records along with copy of the judgment and award and the decree passed.
